## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

import { existsSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync, mkdirSync, statSync } from 'node:fs'
import { resolve, join, extname } from 'node:path'
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
import { createServer } from 'node:http'
import { spawn } from 'node:child_process'
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url'
import { child } from './session-lifecycle.mjs'
import { livePreviewScript, watchProject } from './live-preview.mjs'

export function projectType(root) {
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'package.json'))) {
    const p = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'), 'utf8'))
    if (p.dependencies?.next || p.devDependencies?.next) throw new Error('Unsupported framework: customize start.sh and provide static deployment output.')
    if (p.dependencies?.vite || p.devDependencies?.vite) return 'vite'
    throw new Error('Unsupported package project: customize start.sh and deployment output.')
  }
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) return 'html'
  throw new Error('No generated index.html or supported package project.')
}
export async function start(root = process.cwd()) {
  const type = projectType(root)
  const projectRoot = resolve(root)
  if (type === 'vite') {
    const stampDir = process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR || join(root, 'node_modules', '.cache')
    mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true })
    const stamp = join(stampDir, 'default-dependencies')
    const lock = join(root, 'package-lock.json')
    const hash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex')
    let old = ''
    try { old = readFileSync(stamp, 'utf8') } catch {}
    if (old !== hash || !existsSync(join(root, 'node_modules/vite'))) {
      await child('npm', [existsSync(lock) ? 'ci' : 'install', '--no-audit', '--no-fund'], { cwd: root })
      mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true })
      const installedHash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex')
      writeFileSync(stamp, installedHash)
    }
    await child(process.execPath, [join(root, 'node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js'), 'build', '--base', './'], { cwd: root })
    root = join(root, 'dist')
  }
  if (!existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) throw new Error('Static deployment output must contain index.html.')
  if (process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR) writeFileSync(join(process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR, 'deployment-output.json'), JSON.stringify({ project: projectRoot, directory: resolve(root) }))
  const mime = { '.html':'text/html', '.js':'application/javascript', '.css':'text/css', '.json':'application/json', '.svg':'image/svg+xml', '.png':'image/png', '.jpg':'image/jpeg', '.webp':'image/webp', '.wasm':'application/wasm', '.glb':'model/gltf-binary' }
  const clients = new Set()
  const stopWatching = watchProject(root, () => { for (const client of clients) client.write('event: change\ndata: changed\n\n') })
  const keepAlive = setInterval(() => { for (const client of clients) client.write(': keepalive\n\n') }, 20000)
  const buildWatcher = type === 'vite' ? spawn(process.execPath, [join(projectRoot, 'node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js'), 'build', '--base', './', '--watch'], { cwd: projectRoot, stdio: 'inherit' }) : null
  const server = createServer((req, res) => {
    try {
      const url = new URL(req.url, 'http://localhost')
      if (url.pathname === '/__omgithub/live') {
        res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream', 'Cache-Control': 'no-cache', 'X-Accel-Buffering': 'no', Connection: 'keep-alive' })
        res.write(': connected\n\n')
        clients.add(res)
        req.on('close', () => clients.delete(res))
        return
      }
      const path = resolve(root, '.' + decodeURIComponent(url.pathname))
      if (path !== resolve(root) && !path.startsWith(resolve(root) + '/')) { res.writeHead(404); res.end(); return }
      const file = statSync(path).isDirectory() ? join(path, 'index.html') : path
      res.setHeader('Content-Type', mime[extname(file)] || 'application/octet-stream')
      res.setHeader('Cache-Control', url.searchParams.has('omgithub_live') ? 'no-store' : 'no-cache')
      const content = readFileSync(file)
      if (extname(file) === '.html' && url.searchParams.get('omgithub_live') === '1') {
        const html = content.toString()
        res.end(/<\/body\s*>/i.test(html) ? html.replace(/<\/body\s*>/i, `${livePreviewScript}</body>`) : html + livePreviewScript)
      } else res.end(content)
    } catch { res.writeHead(404); res.end('Not found') }
  })
  server.on('close', () => { stopWatching(); clearInterval(keepAlive); buildWatcher?.kill(); for (const client of clients) client.end() })
  server.listen(Number(process.env.PORT || 3000), '0.0.0.0')
  return server
}
if (process.argv[1] && import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href) await start()
import { startForCapture } from './capture-start.mjs'
import captures from './wip-screenshots.cjs'
import { createRequire } from 'node:module'
import { readFileSync, mkdirSync } from 'node:fs'
import { join } from 'node:path'
const runtime = join(process.env.HOME, '.local/share/omgithub-playwright')
const require = createRequire(join(runtime, 'package.json'))
const { chromium } = require('playwright')
captures.instrument({ chromium })
const config = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(runtime, process.platform === 'darwin' ? 'metal.json' : 'linux.json'), 'utf8'))
if (process.platform === 'linux') process.env.DISPLAY ||= ':' + readFileSync(join(runtime, 'display'), 'utf8').trim()
const url = process.env.CAPTURE_URL, output = process.env.CAPTURE_DIR
if (!url || !output) throw new Error('Set CAPTURE_URL and CAPTURE_DIR.')
mkdirSync(output, { recursive: true })
const transient = error => { throw Object.assign(error, { exitCode: 75 }) }
let browser
try {
  browser = await chromium.launch({ ...config.browser.launchOptions, timeout: 30000 }).catch(transient)
  for (const [name, width, height] of [['desktop', 1440, 900], ['mobile', 390, 844]]) {
    const page = await browser.newPage({ viewport: { width, height } }).catch(transient)
    page.setDefaultTimeout(30000)
    const failures = []
    page.on('pageerror', error => { console.error(error.message); failures.push(error.message) })
    page.on('response', response => { if (response.status() >= 400 && new URL(response.url()).origin === new URL(url).origin) failures.push(`HTTP ${response.status()}: ${response.url()}`) })
    const response = await page.goto(url, { waitUntil: 'load', timeout: 45000 }).catch(transient)
    if (!response?.ok()) throw Object.assign(new Error(`HTTP ${response?.status()} loading preview`), { exitCode: !response || [408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504].includes(response.status()) ? 75 : 1 })
    await page.locator(process.env.CAPTURE_READY_SELECTOR || 'body').waitFor({ state: 'visible' })
    await page.waitForFunction(() => document.fonts.status === 'loaded')
    const start = await startForCapture(page, {
      enabled: process.env.CAPTURE_AUTO_START !== 'false',
      selector: process.env.CAPTURE_START_SELECTOR || ''
    })
    console.log(`Capture ${name}: auto-start ${start.clicked ? 'clicked' : start.reason}`)
    await page.waitForTimeout(1000)
    await page.screenshot({ path: join(output, `final-${name}.png`), timeout: 30000 }).catch(error => {
      if (error.name === 'TimeoutError' || !browser.isConnected()) transient(error)
      throw error
    })
    if (process.env.CAPTURE_STRICT === '1' && failures.length) throw new Error(`Published build failed: ${failures.join('; ')}`)
    await page.close()
  }
} catch (error) { console.error(error); process.exitCode = error.exitCode || 1 }
finally { await browser?.close().catch(error => { console.error(error); process.exitCode ||= 75 }) }

The project must be static HTML (index.html) or Vite. Simplest reliable: static HTML + JS with Three.js from CDN? CDN may be blocked by network. Let's check if we can npm install three and vendor it. Or use CDN via unpkg? Build a static site with vendored three.js module file downloaded via npm and copied into assets. Since static server serves whatever files, we can npm install three and copy build/three.module.js + addons. But `npm install` in repo creates package.json which changes projectType to unsupported unless vite. We could install in /tmp and copy files.

Better: use a local vendored three.module.min.js from a CDN download, plus GLTFLoader if needed. But we can build everything procedurally — no models needed. FNAF-style office: desk, monitor, doors, flashlight, animatronics built from primitives. That's very doable with Three.js, and looks nice with good lighting, materials, bloomish post-processing maybe.

Goal: "nice 3D Five Nights at Freddy's game optimized for high detailed phones like Google Pixel 9". Build complete playable game: iconic FNAF loop — sit in office, check cameras, close doors, manage power until 6 AM. Animatronics approach through building. 3D office with detailed desk, fan, posters, two doorways/hallways, monitor tablet with camera feeds, flashlight. Use Three.js.

We need to design:
- Intro/menu screen with title, "Night 1", instructions, start button. Mobile-first touch controls, also keyboard.
- Core gameplay:
  - Power meter drains based on usage (doors, lights, camera).
  - Time progresses 12AM→6AM in ~4.5 min? FNAF nights ~8.5 min. For a demo maybe 3.5 minutes (~35s/hour). Good.
  - Animatronics: Freddy, Bonnie, Chica, Foxy with AI levels. Simple pathing with timers, positions tracked. Each has a location on map; camera shows them.
  - Bonnie/Chica approach left/right doors: if at door and door open and you're not looking, jumpscare. Door closed blocks; light reveals them.
  - Foxy in Pirate Cove, becomes more active if cameras not checked; sprints down west hall → must close left door.
  - Freddy in dark, moves when cameras off? Keep simpler.
  - Camera tablet overlay with 6-7 cameras showing stylized 3D/2D feeds? Nice implementation: render camera views to small viewports using second camera? Could be heavy. Alternative: camera feeds as canvas-drawn still frames with animatronic silhouettes — stylized CCTV image. But "nice 3D" — use a 3D office and a secondary 3D view rendered into the tablet screen via render target? Could render main scene from fixed camera positions into a render target texture displayed on the tablet, updated at low rate. That's cool and performant.

Simplify: build one 3D scene of office plus hallways and a camera module. Tablet overlay is an HTML element with a canvas? Maybe render offscreen 3D feeds via a separate scene graph area "pizza dining room" built adjacent. Use renderer.setViewport to render tablet view into a canvas area? Actually mixing HTML overlay and 3D: create a tablet as CSS panel with a <canvas> showing feed rendered by a second WebGLRenderer at low resolution (e.g., 320x180) refreshed 6fps. That's straightforward. But two WebGL contexts on mobile could be heavy; better use one renderer and a render target + copy to 2D canvas via readPixels (slow). Or render the feed into the main renderer viewport region? Hmm.

Alternative approach: single renderer: render main scene full screen; when tablet is up, animate DOM overlay with a CSS "camera feed" made of SVG/canvas 2D art — stylized rooms, static noise, scanlines, animatronic eyes. That's performant and can look great. Plus 3D main office. This is likely best for phone performance and looks.

But "high detailed phones like Pixel 9" want quality. We can do:
- WebGL2 Three.js with ACES tonemapping, PCFSoft shadows, a handful of point lights, procedural textures via canvas (wood floor, wall dents, posters), dust particles, fan with rotating blades, papers, desk items, wires.
- Camera view of office: player can look around by dragging; office scene covers maybe 220°, with left door and right door.
- Interactive hotspots: doors (left/right), light buttons, camera button, power indicator.
- Tablet overlay: dark UI with camera map, static, room art rendered with CSS gradients and canvases, animatronic silhouettes (drawn as SVG-ish shapes), panning between 7 cams.

Need proper FNAF vibe: dark office, flickering lights, beeps, breathing, ambience. Audio via WebAudio synthesized (no assets): fan hum, door clank, footsteps, jumpscare scream (noise + detuned oscillators), 6AM chime, phone guy optional. Good.

Gameplay balance: nights 1-5 escalating difficulty, unlocks.

Mobile optimization: devicePixelRatio capped at 1.5-2, resolution scale, dynamic pixel ratio, touch drag look, big buttons.

- Vendor three.js: download three r1xx. Check network access. Use npm pack three in /tmp and copy build/three.module.min.js. Let's test.

I could also avoid Three.js and write custom WebGL, but Three is better. Check if npm registry accessible.

- Left doorway at x=-3.2, right doorway at x=+3.2, both in side walls with short hallway visible beyond and door buttons. FNAF1 office has doors left/right on side walls at ±, lights outside.
- Player camera: yaw limited roughly -105°..105°, pitch ±25°. Drag to look.
- Looking left/right reveals doorway with light button panels. Interaction by tapping door/light button or using tap zones. On mobile: fixed buttons for Left Door, Left Light, Right Door, Right Light and CAMERAS, matching FNAF. Big HUD buttons at bottom left/right. Also 3D buttons highlight. Simpler and reliable: DOM buttons styled like FNAF buttons (two stacked per side "DOOR" / "LIGHT"), plus cameras button bottom center. Tapping 3D office areas maybe also. Keep DOM as primary.

- Doors: physical sliding metal door textures animate down/up. Door closed blocks animatronic entry and drains power. Door lights illuminate hallway when on; seeing animatronic at door raises tension. Doors when closed show warning light.

- Camera tablet: overlay occupying screen, drag/switch cams. Top-down map + 7 buttons. Feed canvas 2D art. Cameras: 1A Show Stage (Freddy, Bonnie, Chica), 1B Dining Area, 1C Pirate Cove (Foxy), 2A West Hall, 2B West Hall Corner (left door approach), 3 Supply Closet, 4A East Hall, 4B East Hall Corner, 5 Backstage. That's 9. Maybe 8 to keep simple. FNAF style feed with static noise, scanline, vignette, timestamp, cam label, and animatronic silhouettes/drawn characters. Use a detailed 2D render of each room: draw backgrounds (stage, tables, hallway perspective, curtains) into offscreen canvases once, then overlay animatronic sprites drawn procedurally when present, with subtle animation (breathing, eye glow). This could look surprisingly good and "3D-ish". We can render pseudo-3D hallways with gradients/lines.

Actually, can we render true 3D cam feeds cheaply? ## Objective
- Build a polished, complete, playable 3D Five Nights at Freddy’s-style survival game, optimized for high-end phones such as Google Pixel 9.

## Requirements
- Build now without asking clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.
- Save small JPEG screenshots for checks (viewport no wider than 1280px) and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Implemented a fan-made “Night Shift” game with procedural graphics and audio, rather than relying on external game assets.
- Used Three.js for the 3D office/menu and a lightweight 2D renderer for CCTV feeds to help mobile performance.

## Work State

### Completed
- Added a playable game structure with menu, night progression, office controls, camera feeds, animatronic AI, power management, jumpscares, win/loss states, and procedural audio.
- Added mobile-oriented styling and performance measures, including capped pixel ratio, dynamic quality adjustment, responsive camera FOV, and touch controls.
- Added the Three.js module locally under `vendor/`.
- Started the local game server and tested menu, office, cameras, and jumpscare flows with Playwright.
- Captured and inspected JPEG checks under `screenshots/`, including `screenshots/office3.jpg` and `screenshots/scare4.jpg`.

### Active
- Finish reviewing the latest visual and gameplay changes, especially the most recent lighting, power-out, and portrait-camera adjustments.
- Run a final mobile-sized browser check and resolve any remaining visual or interaction issues.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the latest modifications in `src/world.js`, `src/textures.js`, and `src/main.js`; run syntax checks and the game server.
2. Verify menu, night start, camera controls, doors/lights, power depletion, win/loss, and portrait layout in-browser; capture and read only the newest JPEG.
3. Check `git status` and report the completed build and any assumptions or limitations.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: App structure, game UI, and module entry point.
- `styles.css`: Visual design, HUD, responsive/mobile layout, and effects.
- `src/main.js`: Game boot, UI interactions, render loop, and event wiring.
- `src/world.js`: Three.js office/menu scenes, lighting, characters, and camera behavior.
- `src/game.js`: Night clock, power system, animatronic AI, and game states.
- `src/feeds.js`: Procedural CCTV feed renderer.
- `src/textures.js`: Procedural environment, character-suit, and lighting textures.
- `src/audio.js`: Procedural sound engine.
- `vendor/`: Locally bundled Three.js module and license.
- `screenshots/`: Browser check captures.

## Important Context
- Recent edits added textured animatronic suits, revised character faces, adjusted menu staging, and changed office lighting/power-out behavior.
- Latest edits updated `World.resize()` for portrait FOV and adjusted power-out lighting; `node --check src/world.js` and `node --check src/textures.js` passed afterward, but no final browser validation followed.
- Changes were made in the working tree; commit/push state was not checked.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a polished, complete, playable 3D Five Nights at Freddy’s-style survival game optimized for high-end phones such as Google Pixel 9.

## Requirements
- Build without clarification; make reasonable assumptions.
- Save small JPEG screenshots for checks (viewport no wider than 1280px) and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use a fan-made “Night Shift” game with procedural graphics and audio rather than external game assets.
- Use Three.js for the 3D office/menu and a lightweight 2D renderer for CCTV feeds to support mobile performance.

## Work State

### Completed
- Implemented menu, night progression, office controls, camera feeds, animatronic AI, power management, jumpscares, win/loss states, and procedural audio.
- Added mobile-oriented styling and performance measures, including capped pixel ratio, dynamic quality adjustment, responsive camera FOV, and touch controls.
- Bundled Three.js locally under `vendor/`.
- Added an SVG favicon and apple touch icon reference in `index.html`.
- Improved portrait menu tips, portrait camera framing, screen emissive treatment, and office lighting.
- Ran JavaScript syntax checks successfully for `src/world.js` and `src/textures.js`; other source files had passed checks earlier.

### Active
- Finish browser validation of recent lighting and screen changes, including office interactions, cameras, power depletion, win/loss, and portrait layout.
- Investigate/confirm left and right door-light behavior; recent checks did not yet establish that the light interaction is working as expected.
- Check `git status` and confirm whether changes remain uncommitted.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue browser checks for door lights/doors and camera controls; validate power-out and end states.
2. Capture and read only the newest small JPEG screenshot; fix any visible or interaction issues.
3. Run final syntax checks, inspect `git status`, and summarize the completed build and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: App structure, game UI, favicon references, and module entry point.
- `styles.css`: Visual design, HUD, responsive/mobile layout, and effects.
- `src/main.js`: Game boot, UI interactions, render loop, and event wiring.
- `src/world.js`: Three.js office/menu scenes, lighting, characters, and camera behavior.
- `src/game.js`: Night clock, power system, animatronic AI, and game states.
- `src/feeds.js`: Procedural CCTV feed renderer.
- `src/textures.js`: Procedural environment, character-suit, and lighting textures.
- `src/audio.js`: Procedural sound engine.
- `vendor/`: Locally bundled Three.js module and license.
- `screenshots/`: Browser check captures.

## Important Context
- Recent edits in `src/world.js` and `src/textures.js` adjusted office lighting and display emissive brightness; `World.resize()` uses a wider portrait FOV and shifts the camera base.
- Browser checks exercised menu, night start, office, portrait layout, and camera UI; latest light-interaction investigation was inconclusive.
- No commit or push state was confirmed.

## Objective
- Build a polished, complete, playable 3D Five Nights at Freddy’s-style survival game optimized for high-end phones such as Google Pixel 9.

## Requirements
- Build without clarification; make reasonable assumptions.
- Save small JPEG screenshots for checks (viewport no wider than 1280px) and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use a fan-made “Night Shift” game with procedural graphics and audio rather than external game assets.
- Use Three.js for the 3D office/menu and a lightweight 2D renderer for CCTV feeds to support mobile performance.

## Work State

### Completed
- Implemented menu, night progression, office controls, camera feeds, animatronic AI, power management, jumpscares, win/loss states, and procedural audio.
- Added mobile-oriented styling and performance measures, including capped pixel ratio, dynamic quality adjustment, responsive camera FOV, and touch controls.
- Bundled Three.js locally under `vendor/`; added favicon and apple touch icon references.
- Improved portrait menu tips, camera framing, screen emissive treatment, and office lighting.
- Fixed missing world synchronization in `src/main.js`: gameplay door/light states now call `world.setDoor()` and `world.setLight()`.
- Verified door/light buttons, camera open/select/close behavior in browser; all JavaScript files pass `node --check`.
- `git status` showed project files, `assets/`, `src/`, and `vendor/` as untracked; changes are uncommitted.

### Active
- Finish browser validation of portrait layout, power depletion, win/loss states, and latest visual presentation.
- Capture and inspect the newest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue browser checks for portrait layout, power-out, and win/loss states.
2. Capture and read only the newest small JPEG screenshot; fix any visible or interaction issues.
3. Re-run syntax checks, inspect `git status`, and summarize the completed build and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: App structure, game UI, and module entry point.
- `styles.css`: Visual design, HUD, responsive/mobile layout, and effects.
- `src/main.js`: Game boot, UI interactions, render loop, event wiring, and world-state synchronization.
- `src/world.js`: Three.js office/menu scenes, lighting, characters, and camera behavior.
- `src/game.js`: Night clock, power system, animatronic AI, and game states.
- `src/feeds.js`: Procedural CCTV feed renderer.
- `src/textures.js`: Procedural environment, character-suit, and lighting textures.
- `src/audio.js`: Procedural sound engine.
- `vendor/`: Locally bundled Three.js module and license.
- `screenshots/`: Existing browser check captures.

## Important Context
- Door animation is gradual: after a 500 ms check, `world.isDoorClosed('left')` was still false though the button/game state toggled correctly.
- A server was already listening on port 3002; a second `PORT=3002 ./start.sh` attempt returned `EADDRINUSE`, but the existing browser at `http://localhost:3002/` worked.
- No commit or push state was confirmed; working tree remains uncommitted.
